cards.back: Change Advisory Board: committee of stakeholders that reviews, assesses impact, and approves or rejects a change before production.
Person responsible for the request and its closure, from opening the ticket through final documentation.
Affected or consulted parties: business units, support, security, operations, vendors.
Ticket → owner and stakeholders → impact analysis → CAB/approval → maintenance window → testing → implementation → documentation.
Evaluates effects on availability, security, and dependencies (services, legacy applications, controls).
Pre-deployment test outcomes recorded in the change ticket and presented to the CAB.
Plan to revert to the previous state if the change fails; must be tested and executable within the window.
Moving ahead with a fix or workaround rather than rolling back, when rollback is impossible or riskier.
Scheduled low-impact time slot, announced to the business, during which the change and its backout can be performed.
Standard Operating Procedure: standardized procedure that makes execution repeatable and reduces improvisation.
Explicit control that permits or blocks addresses, applications, or commands; any modification must be analyzed.
Actions requiring heightened authorization: administrator access, production changes, sensitive operations.
Announced and accepted period of unavailability during the maintenance window.
Restarting a service or the application; can break sessions, certificates, or processing queues.
Old or unsupported application, often dependent on a protocol or port that a change may remove.
Services the change relies on (DNS, database, directory, certificates): recovery is only as fast as the slowest link.
Update diagrams, policies/procedures, and version control; otherwise the next impact analysis will be inaccurate.
Tracking versions of code, configurations, and policies: essential for auditing and rolling back.
